title: Data origins

blocks.heading: Data origins
blocks.text:
Primary data is gathered first-hand for the current enquiry; secondary data was previously collected or published for another purpose. Classify origin relative to this enquiry, not whether the information is printed, digital, numerical or spoken.

Applied example: The researcher can collect current local observations first-hand. Existing records can supply a comparison if their population, units and dates are suitable.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
blocks.repair_note: Restored original full-depth lesson after second review identified card-text overwrite; retained the newer applied example.

blocks.heading: Primary data
blocks.text: Primary data is data collected first-hand for the present enquiry. A learner’s own journey observations qualify; accuracy still depends on selection, definitions and recording.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Secondary data
blocks.text: Secondary data is data already collected or published for another purpose and used in the present enquiry. A published school register or service table can help if its dates, definitions and population fit; publication does not guarantee suitability.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Worked enquiry connection
blocks.text: Differentiate primary and secondary data for a new local enquiry. Primary data is collected first-hand for this enquiry; secondary data already exists from another collection or purpose. Format alone does not decide it.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
